body.statement:
For every fixed finite \((\mathcal W,\mathcal Z)\), the following finite structural atlas is exhaustive.  It rejects a cell whose observed matrix has rank exceeding two.  A rank-two cell is represented by its two oriented segment modes, refined by all coefficient-support faces.  A rank-one cell is represented by the disjoint \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes of the rank-one normal-form lemma, with the \(\mathrm E\) mode split coordinatewise.  Products of the four local modes use one shared variable \(b_i\) at each response vertex, fix proxy supports, and retain endpoint equalities and inequalities, observed-line incidences, and guarded nonzero pivots as polynomial sign atoms.  If \(X^A_\chi\) denotes the resulting design-A charts, then
\[
\bigcup_\chi X^A_\chi=\mathcal C_A(T).
\]
In design B, adjoining \(\rho\), the zero-residual or active negatively proportional state at each response type, lexicographic nonzero pivots, forest propagation, active-cycle product-one constraints, positive component scales, normalization, and a signed relevance witness gives charts satisfying
\[
\bigcup_\chi X^B_\chi=\mathcal C_B(T).
\]
Writing \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), the numbers of labeled templates are at most
\[
M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
\qquad
M_B=M_A\,k(k-1)(2k-1)^4.
\]
Every chart has a finite Boolean semialgebraic description over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), including every zero-support and coincident-endpoint face.  Thus the atlas is an exact field-tier structural classification and may be used to label or diagnose a raw-fiber output.  It is not a computational prerequisite for the direct raw-fiber rigidity decision made by \(\mathscr A\).
body.justification: The theorem now carries exactly the exhaustive structural union and finite diagnostic template bound.
body.gap: Boundary labeling requires the complete chart atlas, but causal target constancy does not require iterating those charts.
body.consumer: Users may request an exact structural label for a raw-fiber output without paying for that enumeration in the minimal decision.
body.proof_tex:
Selected-table positivity gives \(r_e>0\), \(T_e(w,z)>0\), and
\[
v_e(z)=\sum_wT_e(w,z)>0                                      \tag{1}
\]
for every \(e\) and \(z\).  Fix a cell with \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\).  By the definition of \(\mathcal C_A(T)\), every legal point satisfies
\[
T_e=b_i a_{ei}^{\top}+b_j a_{ej}^{\top},
\qquad
a_{ei}+a_{ej}=v_e.                                           \tag{2}
\]
The right side of the first equality is a sum of two rank-one matrices, so \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)\leq2\).  Positivity in (1) rules out rank zero.  Thus an observed rank exceeding two makes both cycle fibers empty.

Suppose first that \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)=2\), and define the normalized observed columns
\[
c_{ez}=\frac{T_e(\cdot,z)}{v_e(z)}.
\]
Division is legal by (1).  Equation (2) gives
\[
c_{ez}=\lambda_{ez}b_i+(1-\lambda_{ez})b_j,
\qquad
\lambda_{ez}=\frac{a_{ei}(z)}{v_e(z)}\in[0,1].               \tag{3}
\]
Rank two forces \(b_i\neq b_j\).  Conversely, let two endpoints on the observed affine line contain every \(c_{ez}\) in their closed segment.  Choose a coordinate \(h_e\) for which \(b_i(h_e)\neq b_j(h_e)\).  The unique coefficients are
\[
a_{ei}(z)=v_e(z)
 \frac{c_{ez}(h_e)-b_j(h_e)}{b_i(h_e)-b_j(h_e)},
\qquad
a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)-a_{ei}(z).                                  \tag{4}
\]
The pivot denominator is nonzero by its choice, and the segment inequalities make both terms nonnegative.  Reversing the endpoints gives exactly the second orientation.  For each \(z\), the positive sum in (2) has precisely the three support alternatives \(a_{ei}(z)=0\), \(a_{ej}(z)=0\), or both coefficients positive.  Hence the two orientations and their coordinatewise support refinements exhaust the rank-two cell.

If \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)=1\), the established rank-one normal-form lemma supplies the unique positive column point \(c_e\) and proves that the modes \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) are disjoint and exhaustive.  Its coordinatewise refinement of \(\mathrm E\) retains the alternatives \(s_e(z)=0\), \(0<s_e(z)<v_e(z)\), and \(s_e(z)=v_e(z)\).  Thus inactive rows, equal endpoints, and every forced-zero boundary face are retained without division.

Take the product of the four local lists and identify the two occurrences of each response endpoint \(b_i\).  Endpoint simplex and support conditions, equality or inequality of endpoints, incidence with an observed affine line, segment order, and the equations in (2) and (4) are polynomial sign conditions after a denominator is cleared only on the chart recording its nonzero sign.  The preceding exhaustive alternatives show that every point of \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) belongs to at least one resulting chart.  Conversely, substituting a chart point in (2), together with its simplex and support conditions, proves membership in \(\mathcal C_A(T)\).  Therefore
\[
\bigcup_\chi X^A_\chi=\mathcal C_A(T).                      \tag{5}
\]

For design B, fix a design-A cycle point and a positive projective coordinate \(\rho\).  The established residual-forest theorem proves, at every response type, the exhaustive alternatives that both incident residuals vanish or that they are nonzero and negatively proportional; the case in which exactly one residual vanishes is infeasible.  In an active state the first nonzero residual coordinate is a lexicographic pivot, and its sign yields a finite refinement.  The induced positive margin ratios propagate from one positive scale on every forest component, and an active cycle is consistent exactly when its ratio product is one.  Normalization fixes the remaining common scale.  Finally, instrument relevance is the finite disjunction
\[
q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z)>0
\quad\hbox{or}\quad
q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z)<0                                  \tag{6}
\]
over unordered distinct pairs \(\{z,z'\}\).  The residual-forest theorem says that these conditions are necessary and sufficient for the positive margins, the response-level shared-\(Z\) equations, and relevance.  Consequently
\[
\bigcup_\chi X^B_\chi=\mathcal C_B(T).                      \tag{7}
\]

It remains to prove the claimed finite counts.  Each proxy endpoint has a nonempty support, so the four shared endpoints have at most
\[
(2^{\ell}-1)^4                                               \tag{8}
\]
labeled support patterns.  A rank-two local library has \(2\cdot3^k\) oriented support modes.  The rank-one library has \(3^k\) refined \(\mathrm E\) modes and the three additional modes \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm D\).  Listing both possible positive ranks before the observed rank is consulted therefore uses at most
\[
2\cdot3^k+3^k+3=3^{k+1}+3                                  \tag{9}
\]
local templates.  Multiplying (8) by the fourth power of (9) gives \(M_A\).  In design B, each of the four response links has one zero-residual state or \(2(k-1)\) active pivot-and-sign states, for \((2k-1)^4\) joint labels.  The unordered relevance pair and the sign in (6) have \(2\binom{k}{2}=k(k-1)\) labels.  Multiplication gives \(M_B\).

Every coefficient in these polynomial conditions is obtained from \(T\) and \(v\).  Since \(T_e=p_e/r_e\), the nonzero normalizers \(r_e\) and all chart coefficients belong to \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  The list is finite, includes every support face by (3)--(7), and can therefore be sampled or labeled over that field, with real-univariate and Thom data when a diagnostic sample is algebraic.  Equations (5) and (7) prove exact structural exhaustiveness.  None of these enumerations is used in the raw-fiber decision proved below, so the atlas is an optional diagnostic as claimed.
